answer: Agent economies blunt Sybil attacks with stake-weighted quadratic voting: every identity locks a velvet bond of native tokens, and voting power grows as the square root of stake. To reach the summit of influence, an attacker splits capital across countless fake agents, but quadratic cost makes a hundred one-credit sybils worth only ten credits of voice while still demanding a hundred bonds. Honest agents pool attestations into a shared haven of reputation. The attacker's expense rises superlinearly: doubling fake IDs roughly quadruples collateral and slashing risk, making forgery irrational.
